glosses: To make something (such as an object or message) go from one place to another (or to someone).

examples.text: Every day at two o'clock, he sends his secretary out to buy him a coffee.
She sends me a letter every month.
Some hooligan sent a brick flying through the window, and the bang sent us running out of the building.

Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.

glosses: To get one going; move to excitement or rapture; to delight or thrill.

examples.text: I don't know what it is, but this music really sends me.
The train had an excellent whistle which sent me, just as Sinatra sends the bobby-sockers.
Darling you send me / I know you send me
Baby you send me.

glosses: To bring to a certain condition, to drive.

examples.text:
“I suppose,” blurted Clara suddenly, “she wants a man.”
The other two were silent for a few moments.
“But it’s the loneliness sends her cracked,” said Paul.

glosses: To dispatch an agent or messenger to convey a message or do an errand.

examples.text: Seeing how ill she was, we sent for a doctor at once.
See ye how this son of a murderer hath sent to take away my head?

glosses: To cause to be or to happen; to bring; bring about.
To bestow; to grant.

examples.text: God send him well!
That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
Let’s be going with all my heart. God keep you all, Gentlemen, and send you meet this day with another Bitch-Otter, and kill her merrily, and all her young ones too.
Send him victorious, / Happy and glorious, / Long to reign over us: / God save the King!
God send your mission may bring back peace.
Good night, and Heaven send our journey may have a prosperous ending!

glosses: To cause to be or to happen; to bring; bring about.
To inflict; to visit.

examples.text: The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke.
Vague notions of this kind still widely prevail, and great numbers regard diseases as things that come arbitrarily, or are "sent" by Divine Providence as judgments or punishments for sins.

glosses: To pitch.
To climb a route without falling.

examples.text: She finally sent the 12a after hours of failed attempts.

glosses: To pursue (a course of action) committedly, enthusiastically, and often recklessly; go for.

examples.text: There is often brilliance in just saying screw it. Acting on intuition. Following the gut. Just doing it. Sending it and seeing what happens.

Why is my first instinct Spain here? Like if I was playing two seconds I would've just instant-sent Spain on this. But I think it―there's a part of me that thought it could've been Italy. But, I don't really know.

glosses: To care.
To call out or diss a specific person in a diss track.

examples.text: But if you want beef, it's war. I'll rip you to shreds and send once more[…]And you think you can send for Aspin? Sort it, stop gassing.

examples.text: […] After closing the door, I shifted to the extreme right and sat directly behind the taxi driver. I told the driver to send me to Pasir Ris by saying "Pasir Ris Dr 12", bus stop" […]

glosses: An operation in which data is transmitted.

examples.text: In the sonification of the PDE code, notes are scattered throughout a wide pitch range, and sends and receives are relatively balanced; although in the beginning of the application there are bursts of sends […]

glosses: An icon (usually on a computer screen and labeled with the word \"Send\") on which one clicks (with a mouse or its equivalent) or taps to transmit an email or other electronic message.

examples.text: Good thing I didn't hit send on that resume; I just noticed a bad typo.

glosses: Alternative form of scend.

examples.text: the send of the sea
thus we drifted, steadily trending with the send of each giant surge further and deeper into the icy regions of the south-west
The send of the sea was driving the boat's head round to starboard.

glosses: A messenger, especially one sent to fetch the bride.
A callout or diss usually aimed at a specific person, often in the form of a diss track.

examples.text: Why you're another bird that's fat again. No competition that's, that's the send.

glosses: A successful ascent of a sport climbing route.

translations.source_sense_description: transitiv: Nachrichten oder Gegenstände in einen Beförderungsauftrag geben

glosses: To send (a shipment) with promptness.
To send (a person) away hastily.

examples.text: The League of One was suddenly exposed and in danger of being hunted by enemies of the salarians. Before any harm could be done, the team mysteriously disappeared.[...]Realizing the threat posed by this rogue outfit, the Special Tasks Group dispatched a team of hunters. When they didn't return, the STG dispatched ten of its brightest operators with broad discretionary powers. Only two returned; they reported no evidence of the League.

glosses: To send (an important official message) promptly, by means of a diplomat or military officer.
To send (a journalist) to a place in order to report.

examples.text: Scores of foreign journalists have been dispatched to Seoul to report on the growing tensions between the two Koreas and the possibility of war.

glosses: To dispose of speedily, as business; to execute quickly; to make a speedy end of; to finish; to perform.

examples.text: Yet, ere we put ourselves in arms, dispatch we / The business we have talk'd of.
the which company of harvest men, being ready at the day appointed, almost in one fair day dispatcheth all the harvest work.

glosses: To rid; to free.

examples.text: But whā I had cleane diſpatched myſelf of this great charge and taſke, I loked not that I ſhould at any tyme afterwarde have any more to doe with this kynde of writing

glosses: To destroy (someone or something) quickly and efficiently.

examples.text: "And our dogs used to tree the cats on our property here, and we'd dispatch them."

So Tyrion hatches one last brilliant scheme in a season full of them, and this one goes exactly as well as all the others, even if it doesn’t look like it at first. He alone takes a meeting with Cersei, in her chambers, with the Mountain ready and waiting to dispatch him.

glosses: To defeat

examples.text: Gareth Southgate's side had little trouble dispatching the side 172nd in the Fifa rankings.

glosses: To pass on for further processing, especially via a dispatch table (often with to).

examples.text: These handlers perform any additional checking and processing that may be necessary before and after a message is dispatched to an object. In addition, some message types are handled internally by the kernel[…]

glosses: To hurry.

examples.text: prithee, dispatch
“Proceed, friend Nicolas, and let us dispatch; for, it grows late.”

glosses: To deprive.
A message sent quickly, as a shipment, a prompt settlement of a business, or an important official message sent by a diplomat, government official, military officer, etc.

examples.text: WikiLeaks did not cause these uprisings but it certainly informed them. The dispatches revealed details of corruption and kleptocracy that many Tunisians suspected, but could not prove, and would cite as they took to the streets. They also exposed the blatant discrepancy between the west's professed values and actual foreign policies.

glosses: The act of doing something quickly.

examples.text: We must act with dispatch in this matter.

During the whole time of his abode in the university he generally spent thirteen hours of the day in study; by which assiduity besides an exact dispatch of the whole course of philosophy, he read over in a manner all classic authors that are extant[…]

A farmer could place an order for a new tractor part by text message and pay for it by mobile money-transfer. A supplier many miles away would then take the part to the local matternet station for airborne dispatch via drone.

glosses: A mission by an emergency response service, typically involving attending to an emergency in the field.
The passing on of a message for further processing, especially through a dispatch table.
A dismissal.

glosses: Faire partir quelqu’un ou faire porter quelque chose quelque part.

examples.text: Mais le duc de Mayenne lui fit dire de prêcher plus modérément, sinon qu'il l’enverrait, cousu dans son froc , prêcher dans la rivière.

Depuis sept ans, la Chine est coupée du monde extérieur, et c'est seulement maintenant que nous parviennent quelques microfilms. On dit que la Septième Symphonie de Chostakovitch a été envoyée en Amérique sur microfilms, mais personne ne nous a encore transmis, par microfilms, des renseignements sur la pénicilline.

glosses: Aller faire prendre des nouvelles de quelqu’un.

examples.text: Il est malade, n’enverrez-vous pas chez lui ?
Envoyer demander quelque chose à quelqu’un.

glosses: Nommer pour une assemblée.

examples.text: Paris envoie tant de députés à la Chambre.

glosses: Dispenser des bienfaits ou des méfaits aux humains, en parlant du destin, de la providence, des déités, etc.

examples.text: Les biens et les maux que Dieu, que le Ciel, que le destin nous envoie.
Dieu nous a envoyé des épreuves pour s’assurer de notre foi en lui.

glosses: Pousser, jeter, lancer hors de soi en parlant surtout des choses.

examples.text: La lumière que le soleil nous envoie.

glosses: Projeter avec force.

examples.text: Cela fait, le gars aux biques alla se poster à un créneau et se mit à envoyer aux tirailleurs allemands des balles bien dirigées.
Mais quand Habib, rendu furieux par un uppercut qui faillit l’envoyer à terre, se ressaisit et fonça bestialement sur l’homme au beau visage, le combat prit une allure saisissante.
Envoyer un obus, une fusée.

glosses: Ouvrir une partie par un premier tir.

examples.text: Allez, c’est moi qui envoie…

glosses: Amener vivement.

examples.text: Envoyer un bon mot, une pique acerbe.
La réplique de l'élève était bien envoyée, elle était drôle.

glosses: Boire ; manger.

examples.text: Quand elle me donne qu'un seul biscuit, parce que c'est mauvais pour moi [un chien], mais que je la vois s'envoyer un paquet entier de pepito.

[…] ; l'autre, son barda sur l'épaule, les chausses lui dégringolant le long des jambes, la tête rejetée en arrière et s'envoyant un jet de sa gourde dans le gosier, a l'allure épaisse et la trogne truculente d'un rustaud des Flandres.

examples.text: Je suis libre… Rien ne compte que mon caprice… Je m’envoie un type quand ça me plaît… Et ça n’a pas d’autre importance…

glosses: Envoyer, faire partir quelque chose pour une certaine destination.

examples.text: C’est du port d’Ambly-sur-Bar que s’expédient sur Paris, le nord de la France et la Belgique, les nombreux bois de commerce et de chauffage qui proviennent des forêts des environs.

Elle avait eu deux beaux enfants de ce matelot, la Clémence, puis la chienne de guerre, la grande, était arrivée, expédiant le Paul aux Dardanelles, dans les pays là-bas comme on disait, aux cinq cents diables quoi !

Expédier son courrier.

glosses: Copier littéralement un état administratif, un acte notarié ou juridique, un diplôme, un brevet, etc., en les revêtant des formes nécessaires pour qu’ils puissent faire foi au besoin.

examples.text: En trois mots, Pierre expédia les petits maîtres hollandais et les Italiens mollassons, avec tout l’irrespect qui leur est dû.

examples.text: Il a expédié son dîner en quelques minutes.

Est-ce que je pouvais encore changer de table ? Non, c’était un peu gros. Je m’installai sur une chaise en face pour, au moins, leur tourner le dos, j’expédiai mon repas et je remontai dans ma chambre.

glosses: Congédier rapidement quelqu’un.

examples.text: Et il fallut que Pierre Volet mirlitonnât encore trois inepties du même ordre, notamment: Un poète m’a dit qu’il était une étoile, pour que la salle consentît à le laisser s’expédier vers le fiacre qui devait le convoyer à Montmartre où il chantait à onze heures, car il était très couru.

glosses: Terminer, en parlant d'actions ou d'affaires en cours.

examples.text: À vrai dire, ils n'étaient tous que les humbles instruments de Si Ahmed, ses secrétaires chargés d’expédier, conformément à ses ordres, les affaires de leur ressort.
Les pompidoliens soutiennent d'abord l'éphémère candidature du Premier ministre, Pierre Messmer, qui expédie les affaires courantes. Mais ce contre-feu fait long feu. Messmer renonce.

glosses: Faire mourir vite.

examples.text: Ces bandits l’eurent promptement expédié.
Cette maladie l’aura bientôt expédié.
